Definition: from G1537 and G538; to seduce wholly:--beguile, deceive.
BiblicalUsage: exapatáō is the word for beguile, deceive. In Romans 7:11, the text says "deceived me." In 1 Corinthians 3:18, the text says "Let no man deceive himself. If any man among you seemeth to be wise in this world."
TheologicalSignificance: My position is simple: exapatáō tells me that temptation is real and so is God's way through it — He never leaves us to face it alone. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
